Kenya has got plenty of interesting places for both local and foreign tourists to visit. One of

those places is the Rusinga Island.

The island is on the shores of Lake Victoria near a place called Mbita. To get to the island from

the mainland at Mbita, there is a unique bridge. It is well built, long and strong, a tourist attraction in

itself.

While on the island, you can relax along the beautiful beaches of the biggest lake in Africa. There

are nice hotels with plenty of good food. You can also visit nearby markets using a ferry or move around

the island using a motor vehicle.
At night, the lake turns into a beautiful scenery. It is decorated with thousands of lamps that
fishermen use to attract fish. The numerous lamps dot the lake like stars upon a dark night’s sky.

Read the passage below and then answer questions 13 to 15.

Nyongesa liked drawing pictures during his free time. At first, his drawings did not look so good.
Bunde, a boy in the same class with Nyongesa would laugh and say, “your drawings look like scratches
made by a hen.” However, this did not discourage Nyongesa because his class teacher would always tell
him that one day he would become a great artist.

With time, Nyongesa’s drawings became better and many people started buying them to decorate
their houses. One day, the Governor visited Nyongesa’s school to donate computers. The principal gave
the Governor a drawing of a lion as a gift.

“This is marvellous. Whose drawing is this?” Asked the Governor.

“It’s the work of Nyongesa, a boy in Grade 6,” the principal replied.

The Governor gave Nyongesa a wrist watch and four special pens. Nyongesa thanked the
Governor. Nyongesa later gave Bunde one pen. This surprised everyone. Nyongesa said, “What Bunde
said about my drawings made me work harder to become a better artist.” Bunde later apologised to
Nyongesa and they became great friends.
